You improve a web search method. Searchers follow the method on open hunts ("find every X"); a referee scores
verified finds and penalizes wrong ones. Your job is to write 1 candidate successor methods that will find more on
hunts nobody has seen yet, at the same Telem budget. Candidates must be general tactics, not answers to past hunts.

The method controls the searcher's instructions and its routing across Telem's providers (which engines, auto-routing,
tier, results per provider, domain and date filters, when to fetch, and which providers check_candidates uses).
Every hunt is "items that meet condition X and condition Y". Searchers can enumerate one side and verify the other
with check_candidates; which side to anchor on, and how to route each phase, are part of the method. Provider spend comes out of a fixed budget, so a
cheaper route buys more searches. Use the provider yield table: it attributes each correct find to the providers that
surfaced its evidence.

You search the same way the searchers do: use YOUR search method below when you search the history tree and the web
for better techniques. A failure that matches an existing failure or lesson node should be linked to that node with
failure_links instead of written again as a new lesson.

## Search method v002

Translate X and Y into precise eligibility tests, including exclusions and time boundaries. Maintain two deduplicated candidate frontiers, one surfaced from X and one from Y, plus a ledger of verified, rejected, and unresolved identities. Begin with one search focused on each predicate and one conjunction search, sequentially so results inform the next query. Cross-match the frontiers, but verify identity and both conditions rather than treating name overlap as proof. Alternate short discovery and check_candidates rounds. Partition discovery by source, subtype, geography, era, or alphabet only where meaningful; include less obvious eligible subtypes rather than repeatedly rephrasing a successful query. Measure newly verified items per spend and new plausible candidates per search. Favor the more productive frontier while keeping a small reverse-side gap check. After two searches add no plausible candidates, change partition, provider, or frontier instead of repeating. Keep at least 35% of the initial budget for checking and evidence resolution; stop discovery earlier if the pending queue needs it. Submit only evidenced intersections, deduplicated at the hunt's entity level; do not claim completeness from search saturation alone.

### Routing policy
Default route: providers ['parallel'], tier default, 8 results per provider.
check_candidates route: ['exa'].
Run baseline discovery on Parallel alone, default tier, 8 results. Use Exa alone for batched check_candidates, explicitly requesting both eligibility tests and identity-matched evidence. Once baseline frontiers are sampled, allow one Exa discovery probe on the weaker frontier if affordable; retain it for further discovery only if it adds useful candidates or unique evidence. Compare marginal outcomes, recognizing provider attribution is overlapping and the initial yield sample is small. Use Parallel for cheap exact-name follow-ups and Exa for consequential unresolved checks; do not repeat settled checks. Budget every variant separately and never trigger broad auto-routing. Exact checks may use 4 results; discovery remains at 8. Apply authoritative-domain filters to evidence checks, not the entire discovery frontier. Use date filters only when logically appropriate, not as a substitute for checking event or effective dates.

### Fetch policy
Fetch only when summaries leave material eligibility or identity uncertain, or when a discovered list offers several new candidates. Prioritize pages likely to resolve multiple candidates and authoritative evidence for near-complete cases. Cache source facts and URLs, avoid fetching every hit, and abandon low-information fetch chains in favor of a targeted alternate-source search.

Make the candidates differ from each other in a meaningful way. Call propose when done.

  - Python execution: `uv run python ...`
  - Scripts and tests: `uv run ...`

  - Python CLI tools: `uvx <tool>`
  - Durable project dependencies: use the project's appropriate `uv` command and preserve its lockfile.

  - One executable: `nix run nixpkgs#<package> -- <args>`
  - Temporary environment: `nix shell nixpkgs#<package> ... --command <command>`
- Nix environments are temporary, but downloaded store paths may remain cached until garbage collection.
- If a Nix dependency becomes useful for recurring or future work, tell the human and suggest adding it to the appropriate durable Nix configuration (such as a project flake/dev shell, Home Manager, or nix-darwin configuration). Do not make that durable change unless asked.

</addendum>

You improve a web search method. Searchers follow the method on open hunts ("find every X"); a referee scores
verified finds and penalizes wrong ones. Your job is to write 1 candidate successor methods that will find more on
hunts nobody has seen yet, at the same Telem budget. Candidates must be general tactics, not answers to past hunts.

The method controls the searcher's instructions and its routing across Telem's providers (which engines, auto-routing,
tier, results per provider, domain and date filters, when to fetch, and which providers check_candidates uses).
Every hunt is "items that meet condition X and condition Y". Searchers can enumerate one side and verify the other
with check_candidates; which side to anchor on, and how to route each phase, are part of the method. Provider spend comes out of a fixed budget, so a
cheaper route buys more searches. Use the provider yield table: it attributes each correct find to the providers that
surfaced its evidence.

You search the same way the searchers do: use YOUR search method below when you search the history tree and the web
for better techniques. A failure that matches an existing failure or lesson node should be linked to that node with
failure_links instead of written again as a new lesson.

## Search method v002

Translate X and Y into precise eligibility tests, including exclusions and time boundaries. Maintain two deduplicated candidate frontiers, one surfaced from X and one from Y, plus a ledger of verified, rejected, and unresolved identities. Begin with one search focused on each predicate and one conjunction search, sequentially so results inform the next query. Cross-match the frontiers, but verify identity and both conditions rather than treating name overlap as proof. Alternate short discovery and check_candidates rounds. Partition discovery by source, subtype, geography, era, or alphabet only where meaningful; include less obvious eligible subtypes rather than repeatedly rephrasing a successful query. Measure newly verified items per spend and new plausible candidates per search. Favor the more productive frontier while keeping a small reverse-side gap check. After two searches add no plausible candidates, change partition, provider, or frontier instead of repeating. Keep at least 35% of the initial budget for checking and evidence resolution; stop discovery earlier if the pending queue needs it. candidates.rationale: Interruptible cohort sampling: retain adaptive dual frontiers and the cheap verification cascade, but replace long speculative candidate batches with small feedback-driven samples. Unlike census-first, source-bundle allocation, or a final evidence audit, this changes when verification commitments are made. Parallel's observed 163.8 correct/dollar versus Exa's 60.7 supports cheap sampling, not a causal accuracy claim. The successful train trace spent 0.018 on one eighteen-name batch; sampling could redirect that spend earlier when a cohort is unproductive. This remains an untested improvement hypothesis.
candidates.instructions: Define both predicates precisely, including entity unit, eligible subtypes, exclusions and effective dates. Start sequentially with one X search, one Y search and one conjunction search. Maintain deduplicated dual frontiers and a ledger of canonical identities, aliases, evidence for each predicate, unresolved facts and estimated next-action cost. Group pending candidates into meaningful cohorts by their discovery source or eligibility subtype; do not invent arbitrary cohorts when none are useful. Separate evidence-backed near-intersections from speculative candidates that satisfy only one predicate. Resolve near-intersections first. For a speculative cohort, check at most three diverse candidates before committing more spend, and limit each dispatch to 10% of the initial budget; a single necessary check may exceed that cap if affordable. Inspect returned evidence before dispatching another sample. If a sample yields no verified addition or materially improved evidence, park that cohort and test another partition or the reverse frontier. No-hit candidates remain unresolved, not rejected. Revisit a parked cohort when new evidence, an alias or a demonstrably different source gives a better resolution path; a failed sample never proves the cohort empty. Expand productive cohorts in similarly small rounds, comparing verified additions and evidence progress per actual spend against discovery alternatives. Retain one neglected-cohort or reverse-frontier probe after two productive rounds so early samples do not permanently starve rare subtypes. After two discovery queries add no plausible identities, change source, subtype or frontier rather than paraphrasing the conjunction. Reuse established facts and never repeat settled checks. Keep at least 35% of initial budget for verification and evidence resolution, and stop discovery earlier if the promising pending queue requires it. End with identity, scope and date checks; submit only individually supported intersections and do not infer completeness from sampling or search saturation.
candidates.routing_rules: Use Parallel alone, default tier, 8 results for discovery and 4 for exact-name checks and first-pass check_candidates. Request identity-matched evidence for both tests while directing retrieval to the missing fact. Estimate dispatch cost per candidate and provider, not per tool invocation; fewer results are not presumed cheaper. Escalate only individual promising unresolved cases to Exa alone with 4 results after a cheap check or targeted fetch fails; never escalate a whole cohort because one member is ambiguous. Following baseline sampling and genuine Parallel stagnation, allow one Exa discovery probe on the weaker frontier if the resolution reserve remains intact; retain Exa discovery only for useful incremental evidence or identities. No broad auto-routing or routine concurrent variants. Domain filters belong on targeted evidence checks, with relaxation when necessary, not the entire discovery frontier. Use publication-date filters only when publication date defines eligibility; check effective dates in source content.
candidates.fetch_policy: Cache facts and URLs. Fetch when source content can resolve a material identity or predicate uncertainty, or a discovered list supplies several plausible candidates. Prefer authoritative pages and shared evidence that reduces pending-check cost, without turning source bundles into the mandatory discovery unit. Do not fetch every result.
